headline: Sterling is about 1.3201 dollars early on Monday in Dubai, back near Friday's close of 1.3209 after a dip in the weekend price, while the dollar index stands at 103.44, near its highest since April 2025, on bets of a Fed rise in December. Oil has eased to about $95 a barrel (about £72) on the IEA's outlook for a surplus despite weekend attacks in the Gulf, and Fed Chair Warsh speaks at 21:00 Dubai.

drivers.title: The Fed
drivers.text: CME FedWatch on Monday 16 November showed a 93.9% chance of a quarter point Fed rise at the meeting ending on 9 December and a 6% chance of a half point, down from 11.5% on Friday, with traders narrowly pricing four rises by September 2027, according to Reuters. Kansas City Fed President Schmid said on Sunday that the Fed has some work to do on inflation.

drivers.title: US inflation and yields
drivers.text: US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October against 0.3% expected, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics on 10 November, while producer prices rose 0.3% against 0.4% forecast on 13 November. The US ten year yield stood at 5.143% early on 16 November, slightly lower on the day, and the dollar index at 103.44, near its highest since April 2025.

drivers.title: Gulf attacks and oil
drivers.text: Over the weekend Bahrain said it intercepted Iranian drones aimed at US radar sites, Iran claimed two tankers hit mines south of the Strait of Hormuz, and Saudi Arabia intercepted Houthi missiles and drones with no damage reported, according to Reuters reports relayed by Fox News on 15 November. Brent still eased to $95.00 a barrel (about £72) early on 16 November after the IEA forecast a return to surplus in the fourth quarter; Gulf tension and dearer oil tend to support the dollar.

drivers.title: The UK side
drivers.text: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 November, its first rise in more than three years. UK output grew 0.7% in the third quarter and 0.2% in September, against no growth expected, according to the ONS on 12 November, and Deputy Governor Lombardelli has said a December rise is in play.

lower: Fed Chair Warsh this evening backing a faster pace of rises or a half point in December, which would lift US yields and the dollar and mean fewer dirhams per pound.
Confirmed damage to Saudi oil sites or tankers near the Strait of Hormuz, which would tend to lift oil and the dollar as a safe haven.
Weak UK wage figures on Tuesday or softer UK inflation on Wednesday, which would make a December Bank of England rise less likely and take support from the pound.
higher: A cautious tone from Warsh, or US retail sales on Tuesday below the 0.2% forecast, which would ease bets on Fed rises and weaken the dollar.
Progress at Iran's talks with Oman in Muscat on Tuesday, or a calmer weekend in the Gulf proving lasting, which would tend to pull oil down and soften the dollar.
UK wages above 3.5% on Tuesday or UK inflation above 3.6% on Wednesday, which would firm bets on a December Bank of England rise and lift the pound.
watch: New York Fed President Williams speaks at about 18:00 on Monday, Dubai time, and Fed Chair Warsh at 21:00. UK wage figures follow at 11:00 on Tuesday, forecast 3.5% against 3.7% before, and US retail sales at 17:30, forecast 0.2%, then UK inflation at 11:00 on Wednesday, forecast 3.6%, with Governor Bailey speaking at 11:30 and 19:00 and the Fed minutes at 23:00. A cautious Warsh or Williams, or weak US retail sales, would tend to weaken the dollar and mean more dirhams per pound, while UK wages and inflation above forecast would tend to lift the pound and help someone selling pounds for dirhams.

feed.title: The dollar has edged higher again before Warsh speaks
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3195 at 18:10 Dubai, around the time New York Fed President Williams was due to speak, to a low near 1.3176 at 19:55 and stood near 1.3183 at 20:30, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from about 1.1012 to 1.0998, so the move came from a firmer dollar rather than from the pound; a firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names a trigger for this small slide, and no report of what Williams said had been found, but FXStreet described the dollar index near 103.50, its highest since April 2025, on bets of a longer run of Fed rises after a third hot core inflation reading, with the US two year yield near 4.85% and the ten year near 5.13%, ahead of Fed Chair Warsh at 21:00 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has edged back up as the dollar pauses before the Fed speeches
feed.text: GBP/USD recovered from about 1.3182 at 13:45 Dubai, after a low near 1.3178 at about 15:15, to around 1.3195 by 16:00 and stayed there until 17:40, while EUR/USD rose a little less, from about 1.1002 to 1.1010, so the dollar eased slightly and the pound was marginally firmer; a softer dollar means a few more dirhams per pound. No report read names a trigger for this small move, which came with no US or UK figures out, and FXStreet described the dollar index as still near its highest since April 2025 on bets of a Fed rise in December, with traders waiting for New York Fed President Williams at about 18:00 Dubai and Fed Chair Warsh at 21:00.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed in London trading as markets turn cautious
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3214 at 13:03 Dubai to a low near 1.3182 at 13:36, while EUR/USD fell by a similar share, from 1.1026 to 1.1002, its weakest in 19 months, so the move came from a firmer dollar rather than from the pound; a firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names a trigger for this half hour, which came with no US or UK figures out, but FXStreet described markets turning cautious on Monday, with US share futures down between 0.2% and 1% and traders still betting on a Fed rise in December, while Saxo reported Brent back up to $96.60 a barrel (about £73) after Iranian drones were fired at a US base in Bahrain and a tanker hit a mine near the Strait of Hormuz. Gulf tension and bets on higher US interest rates both tend to lift the dollar ahead of Fed Chair Warsh's speech at 21:00 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has held steady as the dollar stays firm ahead of Warsh
feed.text: GBP/USD has barely moved this morning, from about 1.3203 at 07:40 Dubai to 1.3202 at 12:38, within a range from a high near 1.3209 at 09:35 to a low near 1.3190 at 10:58; EUR/USD moved in step, from 1.1013 to 1.1010, so the small swings came from the dollar rather than the pound. FXStreet reported at 08:17 GMT that the dollar index had broken above 103 on expectations of another Fed rise, weaker shares and fading appetite for risk, with oil opening lower and then turning higher, while Seoul Economic Daily reported the US ten year yield back above 5% ahead of Fed Chair Warsh's speech. A firm dollar means fewer dirhams per pound, but so far it has only held sterling in place rather than pushed it lower.

feed.title: The market has reopened with sterling back near Friday's close
feed.text: When the banks' market reopened late on Sunday, GBP/USD jumped from about 1.3190 to 1.3208 within a minute at 02:05 Dubai, undoing the weekend dip in Kraken's price to about 1.3166, and stood near 1.3201 at 07:40 Dubai, against 1.3209 at Friday's close. EUR/USD rose by a similar share since Sunday afternoon, from about 1.0982 to 1.1013, so the move came from a slightly softer dollar, which means a few more dirhams per pound. The Saudi-led coalition reported no damage from the weekend's Houthi missiles and drones, Brent eased about 1% to $95.00 a barrel (about £72) after the IEA said the oil market should return to a surplus this quarter, and CME FedWatch put the chance of a half point Fed rise in December at 6%, down from 11.5% on Friday, though no report read ties the reopening move to any one of these.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed at the weekend as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia go on
feed.text: The Saudi-led coalition said early on Sunday that it had intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh and three drones over the oil-producing Eastern Province, a day after the US Embassy in Riyadh issued a nationwide security alert, according to Al Jazeera; no damage was reported. Gulf tension tends to lift the dollar as a safe haven, which means fewer dirhams per pound, and Fed Vice Chair Jefferson said late on Friday that inflation is now his main guide for policy, without giving a timetable for further rises. Kraken's weekend price, a guide to the reopening, has eased from 1.3209 at Friday's close to about 1.3169, with EUR/USD down by a similar share from 1.1014 to 1.0982, so the move comes from the dollar rather than the pound, though no report read ties it directly to the weekend news.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped further as the dollar stays firm into the weekend
feed.text: GBP/USD fell from about 1.3230 at 19:35 Dubai to about 1.3220 by 19:45, a few minutes before Fed Vice Chair Bowman was due to speak, and drifted to a low near 1.3207 at 20:50 Dubai before standing near 1.3205 at 21:35. EUR/USD fell over the same period from about 1.1034 to 1.1023, roughly half as far, so the dollar firmed and the pound was also slightly softer against it; a firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names a fresh trigger for the slide, which came with no new US or UK figures out, while Investing.com and InvestingCube described a dollar near its highest since April 2025 on bets of further Fed rises, with the US two year yield up 34 basis points in two sessions to 4.89% earlier on Friday.

feed.title: The dollar dipped briefly as Fed speaker Logan stayed silent on policy
feed.text: Dallas Fed President Logan, due to speak at 18:40 Dubai, did not comment on monetary policy or the economic outlook, according to Newsquawk at 14:40 UTC, so her remarks gave markets nothing new after she said on Tuesday that at least two more Fed rises were needed. In the same minute the dollar eased: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3234 at 18:40 Dubai to a high near 1.3250 at 18:51, while EUR/USD rose in step from 1.1041 to 1.1052, so the move came from the dollar rather than the pound. No report read names a cause for the dip, and it did not last: GBP/USD drifted back to about 1.3232 by 19:37 Dubai, where it was before.

feed.title: The dollar has firmed again as US yields climb
feed.text: The dollar's dip after the producer price figures did not last: CNBC reported on Friday that the US ten year yield rose about 5 basis points to more than 5.15% as traders kept betting on a December Fed rise. GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3246 at 17:39 Dubai to a low near 1.3224 at 18:23, then recovered to about 1.3235 by 18:38, while EUR/USD fell in step from 1.1055 to 1.1040, so the move came from the dollar rather than the pound. No report found so far ties the dip to Boston Fed President Collins, who was due to speak at 18:10 Dubai.

feed.title: The dollar has eased after softer US producer prices
feed.text: US producer prices rose 0.3% in October against 0.4% forecast, and 0.3% excluding food and energy, in line with forecast, after a 1.4% jump in September, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics; the yearly rise of 6.5% is still the largest since November 2022. A slightly softer reading eases pressure for Fed rises, which weakens the dollar and means more dirhams per pound: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3228 just before the release at 17:30 Dubai to 1.3243 within a minute and about 1.3248 by 17:34, then held near 1.3245. EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1048 to 1.1060, so the move came from the dollar rather than the pound.

feed.title: Sterling has edged lower as the dollar stays firm
feed.text: GBP/USD slipped from about 1.3240 at 13:10 Dubai to a low near 1.3218 at 14:45 Dubai, recovered to about 1.3233 by 15:25 and stood near 1.3226 at 16:10 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1055 to 1.1043, so the move came from the dollar rather than the pound. Investing.com reported on Friday that the dollar index had reached a new high for the year as markets price back-to-back Fed rises in December and January, with ING noting that short-dated US yields are close to 40 basis points higher since Tuesday; a firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound. No report read names a fresh trigger for this afternoon's dip, which came with no UK figures out and ahead of US producer prices at 17:30 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has stayed in a narrow range ahead of US producer prices
feed.text: Oil eased slightly in Asian trading, with Brent at $95.41 a barrel (about £72.10) at 06:42 Dubai, down 1 cent, after President Trump said a deal with Iran was not needed to end the war, which Reuters said lowers the chance of renewed large-scale fighting; US crude stocks also rose 4.7 million barrels last week against an expected fall. GBP/USD drifted from about 1.3231 at 07:40 Dubai to a low of about 1.3219 at 10:32 Dubai, then rose to a high of about 1.3241 at 12:20 Dubai and stood near 1.3234 at 12:38 Dubai, while EUR/USD moved in a similarly narrow band, so the dollar has been broadly steady. With no UK figures out today, markets are waiting for US producer prices at 17:30 Dubai, where a hotter result would tend to strengthen the dollar and mean fewer dirhams per pound.

feed.title: Sterling has held steady overnight as oil climbs on Gulf attacks
feed.text: Brent crude settled 3.3% higher at $95.82 a barrel (about £72.40) on Thursday after Yemen's Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline, the Yanbu oil facility and an Aramco building in Riyadh, none of them independently confirmed, while the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two drones. US yields also rose, with the ten year at 5.10% and the two year up about 15 basis points to 4.88%, and the dollar index closed up 0.27% at 103.19; dearer oil, Gulf tension and higher US yields all tend to lift the dollar and mean fewer dirhams per pound. Even so, GBP/USD barely moved overnight, trading between about 1.3227 and 1.3243 apart from a brief dip to 1.3206 in the thin trading around 02:11 Dubai, and stood near 1.3231 at 07:40 Dubai, much where it was on Thursday evening.

feed.title: Sterling has held steady as US bond yields climb
feed.text: US government bond yields rose through the New York afternoon, with the ten year yield up about 12 basis points to about 5.12% and the thirty year at about 5.44%, while US shares gave up an early recovery from the fall in Nvidia, according to Yahoo Finance's market reports on Thursday. Higher US yields usually support the dollar and so mean fewer dirhams per pound, but GBP/USD stayed within a narrow range since the last update, between a low of about 1.3220 at 19:42 Dubai and a high of about 1.3242 at 20:43 Dubai, and stood near 1.3231 at 23:38 Dubai. EUR/USD moved little over the same hours, from about 1.1056 to 1.1051, so the dollar was broadly steady; none of the reports read explains why the rise in yields did not lift it further.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped as Wall Street opens lower
feed.text: Nvidia announced on Thursday that its chief executive Jensen Huang would step down at once, and its shares fell nearly 10%, pulling US technology shares lower when New York opened at 18:30 Dubai. Brent crude also rose to about $93.29 a barrel (about £70.50) after President Trump said the US does not need a deal with Iran, and dearer oil and Gulf tension tend to lift the dollar. GBP/USD fell from about 1.3272 just before 18:30 Dubai to 1.3223 by 19:20 and has since steadied near 1.3229; none of the sources read names the reason for the currency move itself, so the timing alongside these two stories is the only link.

feed.title: The dollar has eased a little after higher US jobless claims
feed.text: New US claims for unemployment benefits rose to 200,000 in the week to 7 November against 194,000 forecast, up from a revised 191,000, according to the Labor Department. More claims point to a slightly softer job market, which trims the case for Fed rises and so weakens the dollar a little, meaning more dirhams per pound: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3256 just before the release at 17:30 Dubai to about 1.3263 eight minutes later, while EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1082 to 1.1085. Earlier in the afternoon GBP/USD had drifted down from about 1.3274 at 15:00 Dubai to a low near 1.3251 at 17:15 Dubai, with EUR/USD falling in step, as the dollar stayed near its 19 month high on bets of a December Fed rise; no report read names a fresh trigger for that drift.

feed.title: Sterling has edged up as the dollar pulls back from its high
feed.text: The dollar index touched 103.08, its highest in 19 months, and then eased back to about 102.80 in the London morning, which FXStreet described as a correction from overbought levels rather than a change in the outlook, with traders still pricing a December Fed rise after hotter US prices. A softer dollar means more dirhams per pound: GBP/USD rose slowly from about 1.3262 at 11:39 Dubai to about 1.3277 at 14:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD rose in step from about 1.1074 to 1.1095, so the move came from the dollar rather than news about the pound. US weekly jobless claims come out at 17:30 Dubai, forecast at 194,000.

feed.title: UK growth has matched forecasts and September beat them
feed.text: The UK economy grew 0.7% in the third quarter, in line with the 0.7% forecast and up from 0.5% in the second, and output rose 0.2% in September against no growth expected, according to the ONS. Firmer growth supports the case for further Bank of England rises and so the pound, and GBP/USD rose from 1.3251 to 1.3264 within three minutes, then settled near 1.3255 before edging up to about 1.3261.

feed.title: Sterling has slipped as the dollar index hits an 18 month high
feed.text: The dollar strengthened again in Asian trade, with FXStreet reporting the dollar index above 103.00 for the first time since April 2025 as traders weigh a half point Fed rise in December after hotter US prices, and as continuing clashes around the Strait of Hormuz dent hopes of a US and Iran deal. A firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3271 at 06:15 Dubai to a low near 1.3253 at 06:39 Dubai and stood near 1.3255 at 07:30 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1091 to 1.1070, so the move came from the dollar rather than news about the pound. UK growth figures for the third quarter come out at 11:00 Dubai, forecast at 0.7%.

feed.title: Sterling has held near its low through the New York afternoon
feed.text: GBP/USD has moved little since the last update, dipping to a low near 1.3267 at 19:00 Dubai, rising to a high near 1.3287 at 20:35 Dubai and standing near 1.3276 at 22:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD was almost unchanged at about 1.1089, so the dollar has held its gains rather than extended them. FXStreet reported the pound down 0.55% on the day below 1.33, with several Fed officials, including Dallas Fed President Logan and Philadelphia Fed President Paulson, sounding ready to raise rates further after Tuesday's hotter US prices, and a quarter point rise in December now fully priced; no fresh trigger was found for the afternoon's small moves. A firmer Fed outlook keeps the dollar supported, which means fewer dirhams per pound, and the next scheduled test is UK growth figures on Thursday at 11:00 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has fallen as the dollar extends its gains in New York trade
feed.text: GBP/USD slid from about 1.3309 at 17:10 Dubai to about 1.3278 by 18:00 Dubai, with the sharpest step from 1.3299 to 1.3278 between 17:45 and 18:00, and stood near 1.3272 at 18:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1126 to 1.1088, so the move came from a broadly firmer dollar rather than news about the pound. No report read names a single fresh trigger for this step: Reuters described the dollar index up 0.2% at about 102.4 near a two week high as traders fully price a December Fed rise after Tuesday's hotter US prices, and oil has rebounded after fresh attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz dented hopes of a US and Iran truce. A firmer Fed outlook and Gulf tension both support the dollar, which means fewer dirhams per pound, and the next scheduled test is UK growth figures on Thursday at 11:00 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has drifted in a narrow range through the London afternoon
feed.text: GBP/USD has moved little since the last update, from about 1.3318 at 12:39 Dubai to a high near 1.3327 at 14:30 Dubai and a low near 1.3307 at 15:55 Dubai, and stood near 1.3312 at 16:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD eased only from about 1.1143 to 1.1133. FXStreet described the pound as holding near a one and a half week low just above 1.3300, with the dollar supported by Tuesday's hotter US prices, Fed Governor Waller's call for a December rise and tension in the Strait of Hormuz, while Bank of England Deputy Governor Lombardelli said further UK rate rises remain likely. No fresh trigger was found for the afternoon's small moves, the US bond market is shut for Veterans Day, and the next scheduled test is UK growth figures on Thursday at 11:00 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has dipped as the dollar firms in the London morning
feed.text: GBP/USD rose from about 1.3331 at 10:40 Dubai to about 1.3344 by 11:20 Dubai, then fell to a low near 1.3312 at 12:20 Dubai and stood near 1.3319 at 12:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1157 to 1.1138, so most of the fall came from a firmer dollar, with the pound doing slightly worse than the euro. No report read names a trigger for this swing: the US bond market is shut for Veterans Day, no US or UK figures were due this morning, and the backdrop is unchanged, with a December Fed rise almost fully priced after Tuesday's hotter US prices. A firmer dollar means fewer dirhams per pound, and the next scheduled test is UK growth figures on Thursday at 11:00 Dubai.

feed.title: Sterling has edged lower as the dollar firms again in the European morning
feed.text: GBP/USD eased from about 1.3349 at 09:25 Dubai to about 1.3331 by 10:35 Dubai, while EUR/USD fell in step from about 1.1165 to 1.1153, so most of the move came from a slightly firmer dollar rather than news about the pound. No report read names a fresh trigger: FXStreet described the dollar index as steady near 102.20 in Asian trade, with futures still pricing about a 91% chance of a December Fed rise after Tuesday's hotter US prices and Chicago Fed President Goolsbee calling them borderline disturbing. A firmer Fed outlook keeps the dollar supported, which means fewer dirhams per pound, and no UK figures are due until Thursday.
